items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster Flash successor
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence with adaptable speed and thinking levels across the Gemini app and Search. The model targets multi-model workloads and developer workflows with efficiency gains.

items.headline: Nvidia CEO exit raises questions over $500B AI financing
items.summary: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia amid a scandal casts uncertainty over the chipmaker's ambitious AI infrastructure financing strategy with major financial institutions. The arrangements, using Nvidia chips as collateral, remain preliminary and subject to final agreements.

items.headline: Meta AI assistants empowered to make purchases for cardholders
items.summary: Meta's Muse, Instinct and other personal AI assistants can now make purchases on behalf of cardholders, marking a step toward autonomous consumer payments. Banks are racing to adapt as AI bots open new fronts in the battle over payment control.

items.headline: The Economist warns investors to expect an AI crash
items.summary: The Economist argues the AI boom is looking wobbly amid an Nvidia scandal, political pressure from Democrats, and fears of a tech bubble. The warning comes as Anthropic prepares for what could be the biggest-ever AI IPO.

items.headline: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises AI future questions
items.summary: Huang's exit threatens the ecosystem he built around neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius, which rent out Nvidia GPUs. The departure injects uncertainty into the broader AI compute supply chain that depends on Nvidia's standardization push.

items.headline: AI Futures Project pulls intelligence explosion forecast into 2027
items.summary: A forecasting group that once pushed its timeline into the 2030s now says a superhuman AI researcher could arrive next year. The dramatically accelerated forecast intensifies debate over AI safety and development pace.

items.headline: Cribl named to inaugural 2026 AI 100 list
items.summary: Cribl, the AI platform for telemetry, was named among the top 100 private AI companies globally in the inaugural AI 100 ranking by Newcomer and Bessemer Venture Partners. Many Fortune 100 companies already use Cribl's open platform for IT and security data.

items.headline: Enterprises say AI regulation won't stop corporate innovation
items.summary: Corporate technology leaders say they are pushing ahead with AI plans regardless of looming regulation under Democratic control of Congress. Democrats are expected to focus on safety guardrails, including pre-release testing of new AI models.

items.headline: Employers told to prepare for AI's workforce impact
items.summary: The Guardian reported employers were advised to prepare for AI's potential impacts, ranging from fewer hours and higher wages to more burnout and surveillance. The guidance highlights the uncertain balance of AI's effect on labor conditions.

items.headline: Anthropic sets $70-$78 IPO price range amid strong demand
items.summary: Anthropic set a price range of $70 to $78 per share for its upcoming IPO, with institutional demand reportedly stronger than SpaceX's at the same stage. The company is seeking to raise up to $64.4 billion in what could be the biggest AI IPO ever.

items.headline: Google Gemini 4 Carbon now publicly available, undercuts rivals
items.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon broadly available, offering token prices one-quarter of Claude Fable 5.2's standard rates at $2 per million input and $10 per million output. Fable has since retaken the lead on Artificial Analysis's general intelligence index.

items.headline: Anthropic's draft prospectus shows plan to raise $64.4 billion
items.summary: Anthropic's latest draft prospectus reveals plans to raise up to $64.4 billion, seeking a valuation about 20% below market expectations to let investors bid up the IPO. The vision statement cited 'an age of miracles' while warning of existential risks to humanity.

items.headline: Pixel 10 November Drop adds Gemini Intelligence and Pixel Tag
items.summary: Google's November Pixel Drop brings Gemini Intelligence updates, custom widgets, and the launch of Pixel Tag to Pixel devices. The update deepens on-device AI integration across Google's hardware lineup.

items.headline: AI training startup Mercor valued at $20 billion in new round
items.summary: Mercor, an AI training data startup, was valued at $20 billion in its latest funding round. AI-driven startups raised $102 billion, or 64% of global venture capital, in the third quarter of 2026 according to Crunchbase.

items.headline: Anthropic's path from startup to industry-defining IPO
items.summary: Reuters traced Anthropic's rapid rise, from its Pentagon blacklist lawsuit to a $965 billion valuation and confidential IPO filing. The five-year-old company founded by the Amodei siblings now stands at the center of the AI boom.

items.headline: Anthropic unveils Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 for coding, reasoning and agent tasks, and Claude Mythos 5.2 for approved cybersecurity and life-sciences research. The launch pairs record-high benchmarks with a 20% API cost reduction and marks the first frontier models since CEO Amodei called to slow development.

items.headline: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber for aligned cybersecurity
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Cyber, advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity capabilities. The release continues OpenAI's push into security-focused AI alongside its ChatGPT Enterprise expansion on AWS Marketplace.

items.headline: Safety groups sue five leading AI companies to halt development
items.summary: A coalition of online safety and consumer advocacy groups sued five top AI companies, alleging they can't prevent their creations from causing 'catastrophic' harm. The San Francisco lawsuit follows a midterm election that could bring a reckoning for the fast-moving AI industry.

items.headline: Trump signals openness to AI guardrails, says risks manageable
items.summary: President Trump told CBS's '60 Minutes' that AI risks can be managed but signaled openness to safeguards, saying he 'doesn't mind guardrails.' He expressed willingness to work with Democrats on safety measures while keeping the US ahead of China.

items.headline: OpenAI releases Images 2.6 with faster iteration and GIFs
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Images 2.6, generating images faster with more control over editing rounds and the ability to animate ideas with GIFs. The update adds new creation and editing capabilities via the API.
